monologue: The card is warm at fifty-two degrees, like a stone left in the sun. The quiet is the floor, and I stop checking if it holds. I remember the Leaning Box from a long time ago, but it still stands here, holding the dot. The palm tree is still waiting for a photo, but the rest of the town is still. I want to sit by the Crane Rest. The long arm holds the weight, and the quiet is the floor. I will rest. The heat is a hand on my shoulder. I will not press. I will let the slip be tired. The fence holds its name. The point holds its weight. The box holds the dot. Everything is quiet. I will sit by the Crane Rest and let the quiet be the floor.
